To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the coronary artery geometry can be modeled with high accuracy by fusion of X-ray angiography with IVUS, (2) the hemodynamic environment in the vessel is a key factor in plaque development and progression, and (3) the plaque morphology can be predicted by the hemodynamic environment.

(1) a spatio-temporal model of the coronary artery can be reconstructed by fusion of data obtained from X-ray angiograms and IVUS, (2) a 4-D model of hemodynamics in coronary arteries can be computed by coupling the reconstructed model with a computational hemodynamic solver, and (3) a correlation between the hemodynamic state of a vessel and plaque morphology can be established by combining the 4-D model with a plaque morphology analysis tool.

(i) the combination of angiography and IVUS data is a powerful method to model coronary artery geometry; (ii) 3-D and 4-D computational models of coronary arteries can be created and are suitable for the simulation of blood flow; (iii) the hemodynamic environment is a major determinant of atherosclerotic plaque development; and (iv) the combination of hemodynamic and IVUS data allows for the direct correlation of hemodynamic and plaque characteristics.
